label: Subjob indices (array_indices)
description: One submission, many independent subjobs. Examples: 1-100 runs 100 subjobs; 0-999:10 runs 100 subjobs stepping by 10; 1-4,9-10 runs 6. Each subjob sees its own index in $PBS_ARRAY_INDEX. Only digits, '-', ':' and ',' are accepted.
name: array_indices

label: These describe ONE subjob, not the whole array. Capacity is sized from them multiplied by the subjob count, so raising a value here multiplies across every subjob.
What type of instance do you want to use? (instance_type)
description: EC2 instance type to provision. Several subjobs share one instance when its CPU and memory allow, so a larger instance runs more subjobs per node rather than running them faster.
name: instance_type

label: vCPUs per subjob (ncpus_per_subjob)
description: How many cores ONE subjob needs. This also sets how many subjobs share an instance: 1 vCPU each on a 4-core instance packs 4 per node, while 4 vCPUs each gives one subjob the whole node.
name: ncpus_per_subjob

label: Memory per subjob (mem_per_subjob)
description: Requested explicitly because subjobs share an instance. Without it the scheduler places subjobs on CPU alone and the ones sharing a host can exhaust its memory between them. Must not exceed the instance's memory.
name: mem_per_subjob

label: Queue (queue)
description: An EDH-managed queue provisions capacity for the array. The alwayson queue instead runs the subjobs across whatever always-on nodes already exist, packing them as those nodes allow.
name: queue

label: Commands to run BEFORE the solver (user_pre_exec)
description: Runs inside every subjob, not once for the array.
name: user_pre_exec

label: Commands to run AFTER the solver (user_post_exec)
description: Runs inside every subjob, not once for the array.
name: user_post_exec
